title: AsPredicted: lightweight preregistration with explicit private-public tradeoff
summary: AsPredicted is encoded because it exposes a core design tension for the missing-half corpus: making preregistration easy and optionally private may increase uptake, but private records cannot by themselves reveal the denominator of performed studies or results.

status_history.note: Promoted in rev0008 as a denominator-visibility / registration-correction infrastructure record.

claims.claim: AsPredicted describes itself as a platform that makes preregistrations easy to make and evaluate; preregistrations can be downloaded as timestamped single-page PDFs with unique verification URLs.
what_would_change_status: AsPredicted changes platform model or timestamp/PDF/URL behavior.

claims.claim: AsPredicted says preregistrations remain private until an author makes them public; public preregistrations cannot be modified and are automatically backed up in the Web Archive.
what_would_change_status: AsPredicted changes private/public transition, immutability, or archive backup policy.

claims.claim: AsPredicted explicitly allows preregistrations to remain private forever and explains the tradeoff: public-release requirements may reduce voluntary preregistration, but private preregistration alone is unlikely to mitigate the file-drawer problem without commitments to disclose study existence, results, and adequate details.
what_would_change_status: AsPredicted changes private-forever policy or publishes outcome evidence changing the tradeoff analysis.

limitations: This record establishes infrastructure existence, stated purpose, process fields, and design tradeoffs; it does not estimate coverage, compliance, publication bias reduction, or outcome effects.
Registry presence is not evidence that a study was completed, well conducted, published, unpublished, null, or reported without discrepancies.

type_payload.jurisdiction_or_scope: cross-field voluntary preregistration platform; historically prominent in psychology/social science use
signal_capture_model: public immutability and Web Archive backup
reporter_protection_design: private-forever option is designed to reduce adoption friction, not to create public denominator completeness
outputs: Web Archive backup for public records
limitations: no guarantee of study completion or result reporting
explicitly insufficient alone for file-drawer mitigation
type_payload.query_value: Names the voluntary-adoption versus denominator-completeness tradeoff that future preregistration records must surface explicitly.

handling_notes: Registries and post-publication platforms can make hidden or corrected research visible; they can also become instruments of reputational harm if treated as accusation surfaces.
Keep source, claim, study, result, correction, and comment separate. A platform record is not a verdict on any individual study or author.
Private, embargoed, or confidential records must not be bypassed; cite only public source metadata or ethically/lawfully available material.

unknowns: No database sampling was performed in rev0008.
Compliance, result-posting rates, selective public release, correction latency, and field-specific uptake remain open.
No individual trial, preregistration, Registered Report, retraction, or PubPeer thread record is promoted in this revision.
next_actions: Create a study-lifecycle record linking one public preregistration/registry record to its results, publication, and correction/update state.
Add compliance and coverage audits before treating any infrastructure as denominator-complete.
Add negative controls: registered studies whose records did not lead to public results, and public corrections that did not change practice.
